title: A covered face, a carrying voice
odia:
ଓଢଣା ପଡିଛି ନାକ ସରିକି
ତୁଣ୍ଡ ଶୁଭୁଅଛି ଚଉପାଢ଼ୀକି।
literal_meaning: The veil reaches the nose, yet the voice can be heard as far as the meeting pavilion.
meaning_odia: ନାକ ଯାଏ ଓଢଣା ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ କଥାର ସ୍ୱର ଚଉପାଢ଼ୀ ଯାଏ ଶୁଭୁଛି—ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ରରେ ବାହାରର ସଂଯତ ରୂପ ଓ ଉଚ୍ଚ ସ୍ୱରର କଥା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଅମେଳକୁ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏହା କଥକଙ୍କ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ; ନାରୀ ଚୁପ୍ ରହିବା ଉଚିତ ବୋଲି ଉପଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: The saying contrasts a face covered to the nose with a voice carrying far beyond it. Its teasing force depends on the speaker treating the covered appearance as reserved, while hearing something much more conspicuous. Our reading identifies that contrast without making quietness a duty for women.
usage_example: In an imagined reading discussion, someone points out how the covered face and far-carrying voice pull in opposite directions. The group can discuss the speaker’s expectations as well as the image itself. This illustration is newly composed.
cultural_context: ଚଉପାଢ଼ୀ names a meeting pavilion or village school in the inspected dictionary. Here it gives the voice a destination beyond the covered face. A modern fictional use places the saying in a grandmother’s rebuke, showing a gendered judgement in that particular scene.

english_summary: The speaker contrasts a covered face with a voice that carries far.
